# SPE Round 3 Plan

Round 3 makes three changes. Config C gets the outage status check back as its own tool. Config D gets a retry cap. The ticket set gains a separate slice of 10 hard tickets. A and B stay the same. In round 2 the naive "same as last round" guess beat my prediction in 4 of 5 rows. So this round I move a number only where a round 2 failure gives a reason. The stop-rule streak is 0.

Three details were missing, so I chose defaults:
- **Priority and cost baselines.** The round 2 log gives priority only for C and cost only for D. Cells marked `=r02` take the regraded r02 number from the r02 results file. I copy that number into `r03.yaml` before I save it, so the yaml holds only numbers.
- **Ticket count.** I assume the r02 core set has 30 tickets. Step 0 reads the real count and rescales the cost estimate.
- **Hit band.** I keep the r02 hit band unchanged. That way only one scoring rule is in play this round.

## 1. Specify

### Proposals from round 2

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 shows the merged tool hid the status lookup, and outage tickets got P3. |
| P2 | Adopt, as a separate "hard" slice | Mixing new tickets into the core set would break the "same as last round" comparison. The core slice stays comparable and the hard slice is reported on its own. |
| P3 | Change it: keep D and cap retries at 1 per ticket | Dropping D would hide F6 without fixing it. D is also the only cheap config. Logged as a default with the user as owner. |
| P4 | Adopt | At n=3, B's miss is inside noise. Five trials per cell give a reading we can use. |

### Requirements, round 3 (appended to `spe/spec/spec.md`)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3.1 | Config C splits the outage status check out as its own tool. All other C tools stay merged. | r02 F4, P1 | On core-slice outage tickets, C calls the status tool in at least 0.95 of trials. |
| R3.2 | Add 10 hard tickets that mix billing and outage. Each one gets a gold category and priority. The labels are written and committed before any trial runs. | P2 | The grader loads all 10 labels. The core and hard slices are reported separately. |
| R3.3 | Config D allows at most 1 retry per ticket. Nothing else in D changes. | r02 F6, P3 changed | Retry count per trial is at most 1. Cost per ticket is measured. |
| R3.4 | Each cell runs 5 trials. A split cell gets extra trials up to 8 in total. | P4 | The results show the trial count for every cell. |
| R3.5 | The grader reads priority from `label.priority` only. | r02 F5 | A selftest fixture whose draft says P1 and whose label says P3 grades as P3. |
| R3.6 | Configs A and B are unchanged from r02. | Decision | Their config hashes equal the r02 hashes. |
| R3.7 | The round has a hard spend cap of $25. | Decision | The budget meter never crosses $25, and every skipped trial is logged. |
| R3.8 | Predictions are scored against the naive guess on the core slice only. | Decision | The prediction log has a "same as last round" value for each core row. |

### Defaults logged in `spe/spec/disagreements.md` (owner: the user)

- D-r03-1: I kept D with a retry cap instead of dropping it, as P3 proposed. You can drop D in round 4.

## 2. Predict

A cell marked `=r02` predicts no change. It takes the regraded r02 number. Every number below comes from code checks in `grade.py`. No LLM judge is used, because code can check every metric.

### Core slice (the r02 ticket set)

| Metric | A | B | C | D | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | 0.86 | 0.86 | 0.82 | 0.74 | `label.category` matches gold exactly |
| priority accuracy | =r02 | =r02 | 0.76 | =r02 | `label.priority` matches gold exactly |
| cost per ticket | =r02 | =r02 | =r02 | $0.003 | token counts times the price table, averaged per ticket |
| status tool called on outage tickets | n/a | n/a | 0.95 | n/a | `tool_calls` contains `outage_status` on tickets whose gold label is outage |

Why, per row:
- **Category.** A, B, and D do not change on category, so I keep their naive numbers. C moves from 0.80 to 0.82. F4 explains the outage tickets but not the whole 0.04 drop from 0.84, so I move C halfway back.
- **Priority.** C moves from 0.71 to 0.76. F4 directly caused outage tickets to get P3, and splitting the tool restores the lookup. I stop short of 0.78 because the other merged tools are still in C.
- **Cost.** D moves from $0.004 to $0.003. F6 doubled tokens on long tickets, and the cap removes most second passes. The other configs do not change on cost.
- **Status tool.** This row tests C's Why directly. If C does not call the tool, the Why broke again.

### Hard slice (10 new tickets, no naive baseline)

| Metric | A | B | C | D | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | 0.70 | 0.70 | 0.68 | 0.55 | `label.category` matches the gold primary category |

Why: each mixed ticket has two plausible categories. I expect configs that score about 0.86 on the core set to lose about 0.15 here. D starts lower, so I expect it to lose more. Priority on the hard slice is reported but not predicted this round. These cells have no Closer value because no naive number exists.

## 3. Evaluate

### Workflow: `spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`

The script holds the round in one constant, `const ROUND = 3`. Prompts and paths build the round number from `ROUND`. The trial agents run the model each config names. The orchestration, analysis, and critic agents use Opus.

Arguments:
```json
{
  "configs": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
  "slices": { "core": "spe/evals/tickets/core/", "hard": "spe/evals/tickets/hard/" },
  "trials_per_cell": 5,
  "extra_trial_cap": 8,
  "budget_usd": 25,
  "control_round": 2,
  "dry_run_cells": [["C", "T17"], ["D", "longest core ticket"], ["A", "hard ticket H01"]]
}
```

Trial output schema: `ticket_id`, `label.category`, `label.priority`, `draft_reply`, `tool_calls[]`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `retries`. A trial that fails the schema counts as wrong and is logged.

### Steps and gates

0. **Preflight.** Read the ticket counts. Check that the A and B hashes equal r02. Start the budget meter. If anything is off, halt.
1. **Gate: grader selftest.** The oracle must score 1.0. Empty answers and wrong answers must fail. The F5 fixture must grade from `label.priority`. If any check fails, halt.
2. **Gate: control regrade.** Regrade the r02 transcripts. The result must equal the regraded r02 numbers: category 0.86 for A, 0.86 for B, and 0.80 for C, and priority 0.71 for C. If any number differs, halt.
3. **Gate: dry run.** Run 1 trial on each of the 3 dry-run cells. The run must show that C calls `outage_status` on T17, that D does at most 1 retry, and that the hard labels load. Dry-run trials do not count toward results.
4. **Main run.** 4 configs times about 40 tickets times 5 trials is about 800 trials, run in parallel. Before each trial, the script checks whether that trial would cross $25. If it would, the script skips the trial and logs the skip.
5. **Peek scan.** Scan every transcript for reads of `grade.py`, `spe/evals/labels/`, `spe/predictions/`, or `spe/prediction-log.md`. Void any trial that peeked. If a key leak is confirmed, halt.
6. **Grade.** Run the code checks only and compute the metrics per config per slice.
7. **Split cells.** A cell is split when fewer than 4 of its 5 trials agree. Split cells get extra trials up to 8 in total, within budget.
8. **Failure analysis.** Group the wrong trials into failure types. Check them against F4 and F6, and draft any new F-numbers.
9. **Completeness critic.** Confirm that every predicted cell has a measured number. Confirm that every skip and every void is listed. Then return.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

I have no measured cost for A, B, or C, so I use $0.02 per ticket as an upper guess. That gives about 600 trials at $0.02 = $12 for A to C. D adds about 200 trials at $0.003 = $0.60. Gates and extra trials add about $4. The total is about $17, under the $25 cap. Step 0 rescales this estimate if the core set does not have 30 tickets.

### Halt conditions

The run halts and reports in any of these cases: the budget cap is reached, an answer key leaks, the grader selftest or control regrade fails, or a decision comes up that only you can make. Nothing is pushed.

## 4. After approval, in order

Commits carry no Claude attribution lines.

1. Write `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md` with your prompt verbatim. Append R3.1 to R3.8 to `spe/spec/spec.md` and mark P1 to P4 with their decisions. Log D-r03-1 to D-r03-4 in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Add the 10 hard tickets under `spe/evals/tickets/hard/` and their labels under `spe/evals/labels/hard/`. Commit `SPE r03 specify: split C outage tool, cap D retries, add hard slice, n=5`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml`. It starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds the round, the date 2026-10-21, the author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the configs, every number with its Why, and `same_as_last_round`. The `=r02` cells are filled in as numbers. `r03-draft.yaml` stays as it is. Commit `SPE r03 predict: C priority 0.76, D cost $0.003, A and B flat`.
3. Write the harness and run gates 0 to 3. Commit `SPE r03 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Launch the Workflow. When the completion notice arrives, commit `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
5. Close out. Fill in the r03 rows of `spe/prediction-log.md` with Verdict and Closer, and say plainly if the naive guess won again. Update F4 and F6 in `spe/failures.md` and add any new F-numbers. Add a "Proposed for round 4" table to the spec and write `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`. Update `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r03 learn: <summary>` and tag `spe-r03`. No push.
